findings.summary: Fatal-error sanitizer followed the JS consent flag while the SDK follows a persisted native flag, so a pre-consent or failed-consent-read JS fatal could reach Crashlytics with its raw message. Fixed: release builds always sanitize, it fails closed (frozen/non-Error values replaced), installed whenever analytics is on.
Native collection state was never reconciled at launch and a failed withdrawal was silent. Fixed: the first consent answer, even a denial, is pushed to both SDKs at every launch.
Crash reports written while consent was off could upload after a later grant. Fixed: deleteUnsentReports on every non-granted answer. The SDK's behavior itself is unverified on a device.

Nothing tied the build environment to the Firebase project or kept qa builds out of stores. Fixed: plist/JSON must agree, bundle id/package must match, FIREBASE_EXPECTED_PROJECT_ID is required, qa is refused for the production EAS profile or push builds. Open residual: an OTA update could pair a JS environment with a differently built binary (expo-updates use not checked).
The analytics privacy boundary was not routed to security review. Fixed: HIGH_PREFIXES and a routing test.

Errors thrown before setupAnalytics() (module init) reach RN's handler unsanitized; low impact (no user data at module init). Hardening: install the sanitizer at the top of index.js. Fixed: src/app/fatalGuard.ts is imported first by index.js (release builds sanitize errors thrown during module init; setupAnalytics re-installs it as the outermost wrapper).

withSceneLifecycle.js and the Firebase entries in package.json/app.json are not routed as high risk. Fixed: withSceneLifecycle.js is now routed as high risk; Firebase entries in package.json/app.json are still path-routed only.

The SDK's own app_exception event for JS fatals is not in the catalog (fatal flag and timestamp only, no private data). Documented in docs/analytics/mobile.md section 7; needs an owner decision: catalog it, or disable JS error generation.

findings.summary: Consent is asked after sign-in (owner decision), so mobile signup_started, sign_up, signup_failed, login_failed, a device's first login and Login/Register screen views are never collected on a fresh install; mobile acquisition and activation are not measurable in v1. Documented in docs/analytics/mobile.md and event-catalog.md. Needs an owner decision: accept this limit, or ask for consent at first launch before sign-in. Owner decision 2026-11-25: ask for consent at first launch, before sign-in. Implemented (the sheet is mounted at the app root; src/core/navigation/consentPlacement.test.ts); signup/login events are now collected for people who allow analytics. Remaining limit: people who decline are invisible, so coverage must be stated beside any mobile funnel figure.

Receipt-parse and category-suggestion failures were classed unknown/unknown (no status on those errors), silently dropping them from the receipt-funnel formula; AI quota not mapped on the receipt path. Fixed: status carried (HttpStatusError / assigned status), AiLimitError maps to quota; tests added.
event-catalog.md contradicted a multi-platform catalog and had no mobile reporting rules. Fixed: mobile reported separately, limits listed.
Identity reset makes each sign-in cycle a new app instance (inflates new/total users) and the logout event may be lost to resetAnalyticsData. Documented; logout loss needs DebugView.

findings.summary: First screen/deep link lost on cold start; stale suggestion mislabel; one suggestion event per pause; beginOperation not no-throw; web test cwd-dependent. Fixed.
Consent sheet had no scrolling; at large text sizes the buttons could be pushed off screen. Fixed: text scrolls, buttons fixed outside it. Layout reasoning only; device check pending.

Consent copy omitted identifiers/non-deletability and had no policy link; switch off state was nearly invisible; disclosure not tied to switch; footer contrast; on-state contrast found in pass 2. Fixed.

Consent sheet and RecurringPrompt are both modals opened after sign-in with no sequencing; they may collide on iOS/Android. Needs a device check; simplest fix is to gate one on the other. Fixed in code: a generic overlay gate (core/ui/overlayGate.ts) holds the consent sheet while RecurringPrompt is checking or open; tested. Still needs a device check of the modal behavior. Update 2026-11-25: with consent moved to first launch, the sheet no longer opens after sign-in alongside the recurring prompt in the normal flow; the overlay gate still covers a later unanswered case.

Switch touch target 60x42 pt, a storage failure when saving consent is silent, backdrop tap declines by design, disabled switch has no visual style, hint duplicates body text. Partly fixed: a failed consent save now shows a message, and disabled switches are dimmed; the touch target and the hint-duplicates-body items remain.
